[[File:Sara Shakulova with revolutionaries, 1907-1908.jpg|thumb|Sara Shakulova (fifth from right) with revolutionaries, 1907–1908.]]
[[Sayyidah]] '''Sara Kasimovna Shakulova''' ({{langx|ru|Сара Касимовна Шакулова}}; 27 July 1887 — 5 September 1964) was a [[Russian Empire|Russian]] [[mathematician]] and the first female mathematician of [[Tatars|Tatar]] descent.<ref>{{Cite news |title=First Tatar female mathematician: prophet's descendant |url=https://realnoevremya.com/articles/6710-first-tatar-female-mathematician-sara-shakulova |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240721183926/https://realnoevremya.com/articles/6710-first-tatar-female-mathematician-sara-shakulova |archive-date=2024-07-21 |access-date=2025-03-03 |work=Реальное время |language=ru-RU |url-status=live }}</ref>[[File:Sara Shakulova in childhood.jpg|thumb|Sara Shakulova in childhood]]Shakulova taught maths at the Zaraysky Real College in [[Ryazan Governorate]] (1915–1916),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://realnoevremya.com/articles/6742-about-sayyid-shakulovs-family|title=About Sayyid Shakulovs family — RealnoeVremya.com|access-date=2025-03-04|archive-date=2024-08-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812164020/https://realnoevremya.com/articles/6742-about-sayyid-shakulovs-family|url-status=live}}</ref> with a salary of 112-185 rubles, Kazan Urban Female Commercial College (1916–1919), Tatar Aitova School, and L. Khusainova Female School. In 1919–1923, she worked as vice people's commissar for education and head of the Main Office for Professional Technical Education of the [[Bashkir Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic|Bashkir ASSR]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |title=Sayyid Shakulovs: Muslim lifestyle but without hypocrisy and dogmatism |url=https://realnoevremya.com/articles/6742-about-sayyid-shakulovs-family |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812164020/https://realnoevremya.com/articles/6742-about-sayyid-shakulovs-family |archive-date=2024-08-12 |access-date=2025-03-04 |work=Реальное время |language=ru-RU |url-status=live }}</ref> She was a private teacher from 1912 to 1915 and spoke [[Tatar language|Tatar]], [[Russian language|Russian]] and [[French language|French]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Габдульнуровна |first1=Галлямова Альфия |last2=Ильдусовна |first2=Ханипова Ильнара |date=2024-10-09 |title=Сара Шакулова: новые штрихи к биографии |url=https://doi.org/10.22378/he.2024-9-1.68-78 |journal=Историческая этнология |language=ru |volume=9 |issue=1 |pages=68–78 |doi=10.22378/he.2024-9-1.68-78 |issn=2619-1636|doi-access=free }}</ref>

In April 1917, she took part in the [[All-Russian Congress of Muslim Women]] in [[Kazan]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yandex |url=https://sso.passport.yandex.ru/showcaptcha?cc=1&form-fb-hint=2.188&&retpath=aHR0cHM6Ly9zc28ucGFzc3BvcnQueWFuZGV4LnJ1L3B1c2g_dXVpZD0wYjc4NjE1Ni1jMDJiLTQ3YmMtOWRmNC0wZGIzZTBhMTRmMmYmcmV0cGF0aD1odHRwczovL2R6ZW4ucnUvYS9ZQnJMUVZjZmVRYXliZEJCP3V0bV9yZWZlcnJlcj1ydS53aWtpcGVkaWEub3JnJmlzX2F1dG9sb2dpbl95YT10cnVl_7dbd307f963743c476306eecd74bef74&t=2/1755579298/5a1ebe0fd6180615892f7cfc0bc66c4d&u=7134467960047056490&s=f3938ba7c4d46700f33862e74d0452d4 |access-date=2025-08-19 |website=sso.passport.yandex.ru |language=en}}</ref>

In 1923, on the invitation of the [[People's Commissariat for Education]], she moved to [[Moscow]], where she worked as inspector of non-Russian language schools. At the same time, she taught maths in schools and higher educational institutions. From 1925, she was the director of the N. Narimanov Tatar School No. 1 in Moscow.<ref name=":0" /> From 1938 to 1963 she taught at technical universities in Moscow.{{Citation needed|date=August 2025}} Shakulova was a teacher until she was 75.<ref>{{Cite news |title=First Tatar female mathematician: prophet's descendant |url=https://realnoevremya.com/articles/6710-first-tatar-female-mathematician-sara-shakulova |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251107234821/https://realnoevremya.com/articles/6710-first-tatar-female-mathematician-sara-shakulova |archive-date=2025-11-07 |access-date=2026-02-13 |work=Реальное время |language=ru-RU}}</ref>

==Personal life==
She had a mother, Fatyma Aynutdinovna, who was 30 years older than her, a brother, Akhmeta, who was 3 years older than her, and sisters Leyla and Amina, 12 and 14 years younger respectively.<ref name=":1" /> Her father was named Kasimkhan Khusainovich Shakulova<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://realnoevremya.com/articles/6710-first-tatar-female-mathematician-sara-shakulova |title=First Tatar female mathematician: prophet's descendant |work=Реальное время |access-date=2025-03-03 |archive-date=2024-07-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240721183926/https://realnoevremya.com/articles/6710-first-tatar-female-mathematician-sara-shakulova |url-status=live }}</ref> and worked in leather processing and sales.{{Citation needed|date=August 2025}}
[[File:Sara Shakulova family, 1923.jpg|thumb|The Shakulov family (from left to right)— Leyla Kasimovna, Amina Kasimovna, Fatyma Ainetdinovna, Sara Kasimovna.]]
[[File:Kasimhan Shakulov.jpg|thumb|Kasymkhan Khusainovich Shakulova]]
[[File:Fatyma Shakulova.jpg|thumb|Fatyma Shakulova]]
Sara Shakulova died on 5 September 1964 and was buried at the [[Danilov Cemetery|Danilovskoye Muslim Cemetery]] in Moscow.{{Citation needed|date=August 2025}}
